tagline: Open Power for a Brighter Future
hero_kpi_rationale: 14.6 GW of installed capacity with 90% renewable energy, reflecting Enel Américas' strategic commitment to the energy transition and sustainability
company_description: Enel SpA operates as an integrated operator in the electricity and gas industries worldwide. The company operates through the Thermal Generation and Trading, Enel Green Power, Enel Grids, and End-User Markets segments. It operates renewable, nuclear, wind, hydroelectric, thermal, solar, and geothermal power plants. The company also generates, distributes, transmits, and sells electricity. In addition, it provides solutions and technologies for the electrification of cities, such as smart cities and street lighting; for businesses, including energy efficiency and demand response; and for individuals, including energy efficiency solutions for houses and apartment buildings. Further, the company engages in the sale of energy commodities. The company was founded in 1962 and is headquartered in Rome, Italy.

risks.title: Dependence on multi-country tariff regulation
risks.summary: Enel Américas operates in fragmented and potentially volatile regulatory environments across Latin America. Electricity tariffs, concession terms, and grid investment requirements are set by national authorities (CMF in Chile, ANEEL in Brazil, etc.). Any adverse changes in tariff frameworks or concession timelines directly impact the profitability of distribution and generation segments.
risks.score_rationale: Fundamental risk for a power distributor operating in 4 countries (Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Peru) + 3 countries in generation. Moderate but omnipresent language ("regulatory framework" p.129). Stable but structural trend. Category weight very high: 26.2M customers depend on regulated tariff frameworks.

risks.title: Geopolitical risk and regional macroeconomic instability
risks.summary: Enel Américas' diversified geographic footprint (7 countries) creates vulnerability to regional macroeconomic shocks: inflation, currency devaluation, political instability. Argentina and Peru experienced political and economic crises in 2021-2022. These shocks affect customer purchasing power, operating costs, and the value of assets in local currencies.
risks.score_rationale: Presence in 7 Latin American countries (Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Costa Rica, Guatemala, Panama) exposes the company to political volatility, inflation, and currency devaluation. Document mentions "macroeconomic environment" (p.128) and contexts of "economic uncertainty". Trend up: inflation and political instability in 2021-2022. Category weight high for a multi-country company.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and critical data security
risks.summary: Enel Américas is accelerating digitization (849M smart meters, 3,319 charging points, 5G network) and customer data management. SCADA systems, smart distribution grids, and consumption data are critical targets. A cyberattack could disrupt electricity distribution or compromise data from 26.2M customers.
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated section "Security of information" (p.120) in the table of contents, signaling formal concern. Moderate language but explicit presence. Trend up: accelerated digitization (smart meters, 5G, IoT) increases attack surface. Category weight growing for a critical infrastructure operator.

risks.title: Dependence on hydroelectric resource availability
risks.summary: Enel Américas generates 44% of its electricity from hydropower (7.0 GW), particularly in Brazil and Peru. Prolonged droughts reduce reservoir levels, forcing reliance on expensive thermal sources or imports. Climate change increases precipitation volatility, impacting production and margins.
risks.score_rationale: Hydropower represents 44% of installed capacity (7.0 GW out of 15.9 GW). Brazil and Peru are highly dependent on hydropower. Moderate language but explicit climate risk ("energy transition", "climate change"). Trend up: recurring droughts in South America (2021-2022). Category weight high for generation.

risks.title: Increased competition in renewable generation
risks.summary: The renewable generation market in Latin America is intensifying with new entrants and falling costs. Enel Américas must maintain its leadership position (69% renewables) against more agile developers. Tariff pressure on PPA (Power Purchase Agreements) contracts reduces generation margins.
risks.score_rationale: Enel Américas has 10.9 GW of renewable capacity (69% of portfolio) and targets +3.5 GW by 2024. The Latin American market attracts new entrants (Arauco, Acciona, local developers). Moderate language but aggressive growth strategy indicates risk awareness. Trend up: falling LCOE for solar/wind intensifies competition. Category weight moderate-high.

risks.title: Complex post-merger integration of EGP Américas
risks.summary: The merger with EGP Américas (completed April 2021, finalized March 2022) added 4.7 GW of renewable capacity and expanded the footprint to 7 countries. Integrating IT systems, teams, and operational processes presents risks: synergy delays, customer losses, integration overruns. The first post-merger strategic plan (2022-2024) depends on successful integration.
risks.score_rationale: EGP Américas merger completed April 1, 2021, operational integration until March 2022. Added 4.7 GW of capacity and expanded into 3 new countries (Guatemala, Costa Rica, Panama). Moderate language but explicit operational complexity ("merger", "integration"). Stable trend but execution risk present. Category weight moderate.

risks.title: Network service quality and customer satisfaction
risks.summary: Enel Américas must maintain service quality for 26.2M distribution customers. SAIDI (9.8h) and SAIFI (4.7) indicators reflect grid reliability. Prolonged outages generate regulatory complaints, tariff penalties, and customer trust erosion. Network investment (55% of CAPEX 2022-2024) is critical to improve resilience.
risks.score_rationale: SAIDI and SAIFI are key KPIs (9.8h and 4.7 times in 2021). Document emphasizes "high level of quality and network modernization" (p.14). Moderate language but explicit commercial stakes. Trend stable but improvement needed (SAIDI +9.3%, SAIFI -9.6% vs 2020). Category weight moderate for distribution.

risks.title: Currency risk and exposure to local currencies
risks.summary: Enel Américas generates revenues in local currencies (ARS, BRL, COP, PEN) but finances part of its debt in USD. Currency devaluations (Argentina, Brazil) reduce USD revenues and increase debt servicing costs. Inter-country cash flows and repatriated dividends are exposed to currency controls.
risks.score_rationale: Enel Américas operates in 7 currencies (ARS, BRL, COP, PEN, CRC, GTQ, PAB). Net debt of US$5,870M exposed to devaluations. Moderate language but risk implicit in macroeconomic instability context. Trend up: ARS and BRL devaluations in 2021-2022. Category weight moderate for a multi-currency group.
